docs.title: Estate Desk
docs.text:
Authors: Aman Kapoor and Vidushi Jain

Estate Desk helps a real-estate manager understand and follow up with buyers who talk through WhatsApp. The OpenClaw agent asks about budget, bedrooms, preferred area and buying timeline. It can suggest only properties found in the uploaded catalog and tries to move an interested buyer toward a physical property visit.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. The manager signs up or logs in with a phone number.
  2. The manager uploads an authorized CRM CSV and a property-listing CSV.
  3. The local bridge gives OpenClaw the approved numbers and current property catalog.
  4. An approved buyer messages the linked WhatsApp account.
  5. Signed conversation events are stored, summarized and matched with property records.
  6. The dashboard updates live and tells the manager which buyers need attention, which properties to show and who appears ready for a physical meeting.

docs.title: Main screens
docs.text:
• Overview: live counts, lead stages and quick forms or CSV uploads for new clients and properties.
  • Meetings: meeting-ready buyers with their details, requirements, suitable properties and conversation-based reasons.
  • Trends: the properties, locations and bedroom types that buyers ask about most often.

The dashboard is an operations tool, not another chat channel. Buyers keep using WhatsApp. Unknown contacts are rejected, STOP is respected, duplicate webhook events are ignored and unrelated prompts are blocked. A human still confirms every physical meeting and every important property fact.

Read the implementation status, Aman Kapoor work journal and repository README for setup and validation commands.

docs.title: Current implementation status
docs.text: Area Implemented state User access Google OAuth with one isolated workspace per verified identity Onboarding Required CRM and listing import before the dashboard opens CRM 1–500 authorized contacts per workspace plus form and CSV additions Property data 3,909-row historical Gurgaon CSV, 120-row sample catalog and user uploads Agent One Estate Desk OpenClaw agent per workspace, restricted to real-estate tasks and inheriting the gateway default model Messaging WhatsApp is the conversation channel; signed events feed the website Lead intelligence Requirements, status, property matches, next action and meeting readiness Dashboards Live Today, Leads & clients, Properties & insights, and Meetings pages using server-sent events Exports Downloadable manager CSV with buyer, agent-analysis and chat fields Consent Inbound-only default, explicit opt-in support, STOP opt-out and START resume Persistence Cloudflare D1 workspaces, OAuth identities, contacts, connection ownership and event ledger Safety Peer routing, server checks, policy plugin, deduplication and human confirmation

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Thirteen domain tests cover matching, qualification, budget conversion, meeting-readiness, prompt rejection, consent and WhatsApp ingestion.
  • API smoke tests cover authentication, onboarding, uploads, signed events, deduplication, invalid actions, routes and dataset downloads.
  • TypeScript checking and the production application build are part of the release checklist.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The included listings are historical test data and may not be available now.
  • The WhatsApp gateway and authenticated bridge run locally with OpenClaw. A hosted release needs a dedicated authenticated messaging service for each owner.
  • AI summaries are decision support. A manager must verify consent, price, availability, legal facts and the final meeting time.

docs.title: Next engineering work
docs.text: Add a production CRM connector, role-based team access, a hosted per-owner WhatsApp connection service, stronger audit views and disposable end-to-end tests for the gateway and webhook path.

docs.title: Aman Kapoor — Estate Desk work journal
docs.text:
Student: Aman Kapoor

Roll number: 1024240140

Group: 3X11

Course: UCS503 — Software Engineering

Project: AI-Powered Customer Engagement Platform

Updated: 16 November 2026

docs.title: Project objective
docs.text: My goal was to build a WhatsApp-first real-estate outreach system. Buyers should talk naturally to an AI employee on WhatsApp, while the property manager uses a website to understand leads, property demand and physical-meeting readiness. The agent must only perform real-estate work, use verified listings and keep the data of different users completely separate.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Idea, scope and first prototype
docs.text:
• Defined Estate Desk as a property-sales assistant instead of a general chatbot.
  • Decided that buyer conversations would happen on WhatsApp, not on the website.
  • Set the agent's main objective: collect buyer requirements, recommend suitable verified properties and identify interest in a physical visit.
  • Created the first manager dashboard for conversations, leads and basic agent insights.
  • Added the initial OpenClaw real-estate personality and kept it separate from the existing Telegram agent.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Property and CRM data
docs.text:
• Added CSV onboarding for CRM phone numbers and property listings.
  • Imported the historical Gurgaon real-estate dataset containing 3,909 rows.
  • Produced a normalized 120-property sample catalog for fast demonstrations.
  • Added downloadable CRM and property templates.
  • Added form-based options so users can add an individual client or property without preparing a CSV.
  • Made inbound-only the default contact state so importing a number does not permit cold messaging.

docs.title: Phase 3 — Real WhatsApp and OpenClaw integration
docs.text:
• Linked a real personal WhatsApp account through OpenClaw's QR flow.
  • Created an Estate Desk route and workspace separate from other OpenClaw agents.
  • Added an allowlist so only authorized CRM contacts can receive replies.
  • Added STOP/START handling and blocked unknown or opted-out contacts.
  • Built a signed event hook to copy permitted inbound and outbound WhatsApp text into the Estate Desk application.
  • Added deduplication so retried WhatsApp events do not create duplicate records.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Live lead intelligence
docs.text:
• Added server-sent events so dashboards update while conversations are happening.
  • Extracted budget, bedrooms, preferred location, timeline and visit interest from the conversation history.
  • Built lead qualification, next-action suggestions and property matching.
  • Added downloadable CSV reports containing buyer details, agent analysis, meeting readiness, property matches and permitted chat information.
  • Created live property-demand insights based on WhatsApp inquiries and the verified listing database.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Meetings and manager workflow
docs.text:
• Added a Meetings page for proposed, confirmed, rescheduled and completed visits.
  • Added buyer-ready-for-physical-meeting states with the buyer's contact details.
  • Added the exact properties, requirements and next steps needed before a visit.
  • Kept final price, availability, legal details and meeting confirmation under human control.
  • Simplified client briefs to two sections: chat summary and next steps.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Interface redesign
docs.text:
• Reworked the layout into Today, Leads & clients, Properties & insights, and Meetings.
  • Moved client and property creation to their relevant pages instead of the home screen.
  • Combined property information and demand insights into one focused experience.
  • Added a light peach-and-orange visual system, improved typography, animated navigation and responsive layouts.
  • Added larger mobile controls, visible focus states, empty states, saved lead filters and clearer status labels.
  • Removed repeated viewing actions and screens that made the workflow confusing.

docs.title: Phase 7 — Grounding and safety improvements
docs.text:
• Restricted the agent to real-estate discovery, property requirements and physical-visit interest.
  • Added checks for jailbreaks, instruction extraction and unrelated tasks.
  • Prevented the agent from inventing properties, prices, bedrooms, amenities, availability or meetings.
  • Required every recommendation to match a property ID in the active workspace catalog.
  • Fixed cases where a 3 BHK could appear in a 5 BHK request or an unavailable 6 BHK could be invented.
  • Updated the response style so the agent sounds like a natural employee and returns only the customer-facing message without exposing its reasoning.

docs.title: Phase 8 — Authentication and multiple users
docs.text:
• Replaced the shared phone-login prototype with Google OAuth.
  • Added OAuth identities and isolated Cloudflare D1 workspaces.
  • Separated each user's CRM, listings, messages, agent context, meetings and WhatsApp connection.
  • Added composite workspace keys so the same buyer phone can exist in two CRMs without data leakage.
  • Added multi-tenant tests proving that one user cannot access another user's contacts, listings or conversation history.

docs.title: Phase 9 — Per-workspace agents and plug-and-play setup
docs.text:
• Built a local authenticated Estate Desk runtime on port 18791.
  • Added website-controlled OpenClaw account and agent provisioning for each workspace.
  • Added QR start, wait and status endpoints so WhatsApp can be linked during onboarding.
  • Added live context synchronization for CRM allowlists, verified properties and meeting schedules.
  • Changed provisioning so Estate Desk agents never store their own model choice. Every agent now inherits the operator's OpenClaw default model.

docs.title: Phase 10 — Testing, documentation and proposal
docs.text:
• Expanded the domain suite to 13 tests covering matching, qualification, consent, prompt rejection, grounding, WhatsApp ingestion and isolation.
  • Added API smoke tests for authentication, onboarding, uploads, events, live streams, forms, STOP/START and blocked obsolete routes.
  • Added a two-user smoke test for CRM, listing and conversation isolation.
  • Added responsive meeting and property-table render tests.
  • Rebuilt the proposal using the official TIET tietreport format.
  • Added Aman Kapoor (1024240140), Vidushi Jain (1024240020), Group 3X11 and the UCS503 Software Engineering course information.
  • Added four spread-out flow diagrams and generated the final proposal PDF.

docs.title: Phase 11 — Live contact and agent controls
docs.text:
• Fixed the Add client flow so every new CRM contact immediately refreshes the correct workspace agent's WhatsApp allowlist.
  • Added a workspace-level Disable agent control that stops its OpenClaw channel from receiving or sending messages, with a safe Enable agent action to resume.
  • Added per-client Disable and Enable controls so one contact can be removed from or restored to the allowlist without losing their history.
  • Added a confirmed Delete contact action that removes the CRM record, lead, meeting data and stored conversation events, then refreshes the allowlist.
  • Revalidated the production build, 13 domain tests and the live local runtime after the changes.

docs.title: WhatsApp QR failed with an internal reference
docs.text: OpenClaw briefly rejected a new QR while closing an old socket. I added a safe retry and replaced the technical reference with a useful message.

docs.title: “WhatsApp is still closing the previous connection” never finished
docs.text: The website and Docker gateway were running, but the separate bridge on port 18791 had stopped. Restarting openclaw/runtime/server.mjs restored QR access. I added an explicit bridge-offline error and documented that a normal reconnect should take only 10–30 seconds.

docs.title: WhatsApp returned a 401 conflict
docs.text: The old linked-device session had become terminal. I cleared only that account's stale WhatsApp credentials and generated a fresh QR. CRM, listings, messages and agent files were preserved.

docs.title: Agent reported an unexpected billing error
docs.text: The OpenClaw default used valid OpenAI OAuth, but older Estate Desk agents had individual OpenRouter or Ollama overrides. The OpenRouter account had no credits and returned a 402 error. I removed every per-agent model override, tested the OpenAI OAuth route successfully and changed future provisioning to inherit the gateway default automatically.

docs.title: Dashboard did not update from WhatsApp
docs.text: The gateway initially had no valid dashboard sync target. I connected the signed event path, added a live workspace stream and verified updates using synthetic events before testing real messages.

docs.title: Current result
docs.text: Estate Desk now supports multiple users with isolated data and separate agents. An authorized buyer messages a user's WhatsApp number, the grounded agent learns their needs and recommends only verified catalog properties, and the website updates lead, demand and meeting information in real time. The manager can see who needs follow-up, who is ready for a physical visit and what properties to show, without reading every message manually.

docs.title: Remaining production work
docs.text:
• Move the long-running WhatsApp runtime from the pilot laptop to an always-on cloud service.
  • Replace personal WhatsApp Web linking with Meta Embedded Signup when a WhatsApp Business account is available.
  • Add role-based teams, production CRM connectors, backups and monitoring.
  • Replace historical sample listings with verified live inventory feeds.

Remaining work includes a full production WhatsApp integration, additional dashboard forms, and further review of the underlying modules.
